description: We are Viento Estelar, a team of high school students from CPES 14 in Pico Truncado, Santa Cruz, Argentina. We are curious, creative and motivated to learn and excited to build something meaningful together. Our interests include space science, programming, data analysis, design and Earth observation.
summary:
NASA Earth Jukebox SurPolaris is a web-based jukebox that uses both images and sound to show how a specific place on Earth has changed between two dates. Users can also upload a satellite image of any location to hear its associated sound. The musical 
interpretation translates the environmental changes occurring between both dates, making it possible for blind and visually impaired people to perceive climate change.  
It presents two case studies from Argentine Patagonia: the wildfire in northeastern 
Chubut (January 1 and 11, 2022) and the retreat of the Upsala Glacier (2008 and 
2011). Each case includes two satellite images, one before and one after.
details:
Project Details pdf: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1LxpQhu7eBvu5i-MNo5KGvNs7p3JH9x7W/view?usp=sharing

Core Functionality

It presents two case studies from Argentine Patagonia: the wildfire in northeastern Chubut (January 1 and 11, 2022) and the retreat of the Upsala Glacier (2008 and 2011). Each case includes two satellite images, one before and one after.

Technical Scope

The jukebox is a single, self-contained HTML file with 4 images and 16 audio tracks embedded directly inside. It requires no installation, external server, or internet connection to operate. The system can be controlled via UI buttons, keyboard shortcuts, or voice commands, with voice recognition enabled by default upon launch. Every action supports all three input methods unless otherwise indicated.

Playback

● A yellow scanline sweeps across the image from left to right in sync with the audio duration.

● Clicking Audio Legend pauses the image's audio so that both do not play at the same time.

● The volume slider ranges from 0% to 150%; recorded audio tracks reach a maximum of 100%.

● The speed slider ranges from 0.5× to 3× and adjusts the audio playback speed.

Languages

● The jukebox launches in the browser's default language and remembers the user's last selection.

● Switching languages updates all interface text, voice recognition, and audio tracks.

● The audio for the currently selected image restarts in the newly chosen language.

Voice Control

● It is enabled by default in both languages and listens continuously.

● It detects single keywords within a spoken phrase, ignoring capitalization and accents.

● While the Audio Legend is playing, the microphone is muted so the recording does not trigger voice commands.

● It ignores commands for the image that is already playing so the audio itself does not restart it. Accessibility.

● All controls are reachable via the Tab key and display a yellow outline when focused. ● Every image includes an alternative text description for screen readers in both languages.

● Status and voice messages are announced to screen readers whenever they change.

Development Tools & Technical Specifications

The entire project is encapsulated in a single 30 MB HTML file containing all the code (HTML, CSS, and JavaScript), along with 4 images and 16 audio files, requiring no external libraries or servers. While the jukebox codebase was generated by Anthropic's AI assistant, Claude, based on the creators' specifications, all core intellectual work remains exclusively theirs. Specifically, the scientific direction, satellite data selection, audio recordings, and final validation were entirely executed by the project's authors—a critical distinction for scientific and technological funding calls.
